questions: Is a database query or network request made once per item inside a loop (the N+1 problem), where one query could load everything?
Does a request handler do slow or blocking work (reading files synchronously, large loops, loading every row) on every request?

hints.title: Database or network call inside a loop
hints.why: It runs once for every item, so 100 items means 100 trips to the database or network, and the page gets slower as data grows.
hints.fix: Load everything in one call before the loop (a JOIN, or WHERE id IN (...)), then match the results up in code.
hints.comment: This makes one call per item in the loop. Could it load them all in one query instead?

hints.title: Blocking file or process call in a request handler
hints.why: While it runs, the server can't answer anyone else's request.
hints.fix: Use the async version (for example await fs.promises.readFile) or do it once at startup.
hints.comment: This blocks the server while it runs. Could it use the async version, or load once at startup?
